text:
maria: heads up — we're seeing SSO logins where users get created but no RBAC role is assigned. JIT provisioning completes but role shows as 'none'.

sanjay: saw a spike in auth failures in the audit logs, digging now. did anyone change the Okta app mappings today?

lex: I rolled a tiny mapping tweak this morning to rename 'engineer' -> 'platform_engineer' for the new RBAC refactor. Could be related. @sanjay can you check mapping hits?

okta-bot: Provisioning event: user.create(joanne@acme.com) status=SUCCESS, assigned_group_count=0

maria: exact symptom — user exists in idp and in our users table, but no roles. auth log shows SAML assertion delivered but our identity service logs `missing_role_attribute`.

lex: that matches — my rename removed the legacy `role` attribute and replaced with `roles_v2`. JIT expects `role` still. my bad.

sanjay: confirmed. 14/42 recent creates had assertions without `role`. The assertion payloads have `roles_v2: ["platform_engineer"]` and no `role`.

iam-service: Identity service: rejecting mapping fallback. Current behavior: if `role` attr absent -> assign none. Suggest fallback to first element of `roles_v2` or map alias.

maria: we need a quick fix. two options: revert Okta app mapping to emit `role` again, or patch identity service to accept `roles_v2`. Revert is fastest.

lex: I can revert app mapping now. Reverting will re-add `role` attribute as string. Will roll back in Okta app config.

oncall-sre: flagging as sev-2 until roles stable across logins. Can we limit impact surface — maybe a default `reader` role for JIT until mapping fixed?

sanjay: default role would be safer long-term but risky for privilege creep. prefer revert then add compatibility in identity service with a short-lived feature flag.

lex: reverted mapping in Okta, pushed new assertion with `role: platform_engineer` for a test user. maria can you validate?

maria: test user now has role assigned. Existing users created during window still have none though. We should run a backfill scanning users with roles_v2 and assign role accordingly.

iam-service: backfill plan: query users where role=null AND metadata.saml.roles_v2 exists, then set role to roles_v2[0]. We'll run in dry-run and post results. Needs KMS key access since we'll write audit events encrypted.

maria: note to audit: capture pre/post role, actor=automation/backfill, ticket linked. Also add log lines to external audit store (we use KMS-enc wrapped logs).

oncall-sre: okta audit shows mapping change at 1765117400 by lex. tagging incident. if backfill starts, coordinate maintenance window?

lex: backfill won't touch production traffic, I'll coordinate a brief freeze for role writes (5m) to avoid races. planning dry-run now.

sanjay: also opened a vuln/ops note — the RBAC rename should have had a migration plan. we need a checklist: update Okta mapping, update JIT compatibility, update console role dropdowns, backfill users, update docs.

maria: agreed. I'll create the checklist and link to the PR that made the rename. Assigning follow-ups: lex for Okta change (done), sanjay for backfill script + audit (in progress), iam-service for compat patch behind flag.

okta-bot: Alert: inactivity on mapping change remediation > 30m. 

maria: closing loop — patch landed in IAM to accept `roles_v2` fallback behind flag. sanjay ran dry-run and identified 28 users to backfill. running backfill now. will post summary when done. :thumbsup:

iam-service: Backfill finished (dry-run->commit): 28 users updated, 28 audit events written, all KMS-wrapped. No anomalies.

maria: thanks team. follow-up items: add migration checklist to repo, schedule a postmortem for the release process that allowed this, and add an automatic test that checks SAML attribute presence in CI for Okta changes.

lex: noted. I'll add the test and link the PR. sorry for the noise, learned to add compatibility layer first.

oncall-sre: marking incident resolved. closing thread.
